question: She ___ to school by bus every day.
why: A daily habit uses the present simple, and a singular subject takes goes.

question: Passengers ___ wear a seat belt; it is the law.
why: Must shows a rule or obligation.

question: By the time we reached the station, the train ___.
why: The train left before we arrived, so the earlier action takes the past perfect.

question: Ravi ___ his homework since four o'clock and is still at it.
why: Since with an action still going on needs the present perfect continuous.

question: I would have called you if I ___ your number.
why: A third conditional (unreal past) pairs would have with the past perfect in the if clause.

question: Which sentence is correct?
a: By next March, Meera has taught here for ten years.
b: By next March, Meera will have taught here for ten years.
c: By next March, Meera will teach here for ten years.
d: By next March, Meera would taught here for ten years.
why: By a future time with a completed span takes the future perfect.

question: Each of the boys ___ a prize.
why: Each is singular, so it takes has.

question: She drank ___ water and felt better.
why: Water is uncountable, so a little is used; a few and many are for countable nouns.

question: Neither the teacher nor the students ___ aware of the change.
why: With neither...nor the verb agrees with the nearer subject, students, which is plural.

question: He has ___ friends in the new city, so he often feels lonely.
why: Few means hardly any and carries a negative sense; a few would mean some.

question: The number of stray dogs in our colony ___ risen, while a number of residents ___ complained.
why: The number of takes a singular verb; a number of means several and takes a plural verb.

question: Bread and butter ___ my usual breakfast.
why: Bread and butter is thought of as one dish, so the verb is singular.

question: He said, "I am tired." He said that he ___ tired.
why: The present tense moves back to the past in reported speech.

question: She said to me, "Close the door." She ___ me to close the door.
why: A command is reported with told or asked plus to.

question: Rohan said, "I will meet you tomorrow." Rohan said that he would meet me ___.
why: Tomorrow becomes the next day in reported speech.

question: The teacher asked, "Have you finished the exercise?" The teacher asked whether I ___ the exercise.
why: A yes-no question is reported with whether or if, and the present perfect becomes the past perfect.

question: She said, "I have been waiting here since morning." She said that she ___ there since morning.
why: The present perfect continuous changes to the past perfect continuous.

question: "Let's go for a walk," said Kabir. Which is the correct report?
a: Kabir said to go for a walk.
b: Kabir suggested going for a walk.
c: Kabir ordered us going for a walk.
d: Kabir asked that let us go for a walk.
why: Let's is a suggestion, reported with suggested.

question: Passive of "The cook prepares dinner."
b: Dinner was prepared by the cook.
c: Dinner is prepared by the cook.
d: Dinner is preparing by the cook.
why: Present simple becomes is or are plus the past participle.

question: The letter ___ yesterday.
why: Yesterday needs the past passive, was written.

question: Passive of "They are repairing the road."
a: The road is being repaired by them.
b: The road is repaired by them.
c: The road was being repaired by them.
d: The road has been repaired by them.
why: Present continuous becomes is or are being plus the past participle.

question: In "I know that he is honest", the clause "that he is honest" is a
why: It is the object of know, so it works as a noun.

question: Which sentence has an adverb clause of reason?
a: The match that was cancelled was ours.
b: I wonder whether the match will be held.
c: Because it rained, the match was cancelled.
d: He told me that the match was cancelled.
why: Because it rained tells why the match was cancelled.

question: Passive of "Who wrote this poem?"
a: By whom is this poem written?
b: Who has this poem been written?
c: By whom this poem was written?
d: By whom was this poem written?
why: The simple past becomes was plus the past participle, and who becomes by whom.

question:
Passage: The village of Kharsi had one well, and it was running dry. Instead of blaming the weather, Meena called a meeting. "Every roof here can catch rain," she said. Within a year forty rooftops fed pipes into pits near the well, and by the next monsoon the well was full again.

What does the passage suggest about Meena?
a: She is afraid of the weather
b: She is practical and takes the lead
why: She skipped blaming and acted with a workable plan.

question:
Passage: Arjun looked at the clock, then at the empty chair beside him, and finally put the second cup of tea back on the tray.

What can be inferred?
d: He was expecting someone who did not come.
why: The second cup and empty chair show he waited for a guest who did not arrive.

question: A diary entry is written in the ___ person.
why: A diary records your own thoughts, so it uses I.

question: A formal letter that begins "Dear Sir" should end with
why: Dear Sir pairs with Yours faithfully.

question: Which is NOT part of the format of a formal letter?
c: A pet name for the receiver
why: Formal letters stay impersonal and have no pet names.

question: A paragraph on "The Importance of Sleep" should begin with
d: a topic sentence stating the main idea
why: A good paragraph opens with a sentence that states its central idea.

question: Which opening best suits a 150-word school magazine article on a plastic ban?
a: A catchy title, a byline and a strong first line
why: Articles carry a title and byline and open with a hook.

question: In a letter to the Editor, the subject line comes
b: after the salutation and before the body
why: The usual order is address, date, receiver, salutation, subject, body, closing.
